title: Staff Product Manager - Measurement & Reporting
text:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co http://Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co http://Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co http://Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co http://Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

About the Role

You’ll own Measurement & Reporting at Vibe: how advertisers find out what their CTV spend actually did.

Most measurement in advertising is built to make the seller look good. Walled gardens grade their own homework, and clients have learned to discount the numbers. We want to do the opposite: give advertisers the most accurate read we can on what CTV drove for their business, including when the answer is less flattering than they hoped. We believe that’s how you earn more budget, and keep it.

You’ll own the strategy and roadmap for how Vibe measures and reports outcomes across verticals. Your main focus will be ecom and CPG, with growing coverage of apps, local, and travel. With Walmart’s purchase data now part of the platform, measurement is becoming one of Vibe’s biggest differentiators.

The Team

 - You’ll report directly to Varun Himamshu.

 - You’ll be the first hire in a new domain. You’ll define it, not inherit it.

 - Dedicated engineering is planned for Measurement & Reporting.

 - You’ll partner closely with our incoming Head of Marketing Science, as well as Data Science, Data Platform, Engineering, and our client-facing teams (CS, Sales, TAM).

What You’ll Do

Measurement Products

 - Build Vibe’s attribution, incrementality, and MMM-facing products to a client-grade standard, not just an internal signal.

 - Decide which method answers which question, and be explicit with clients about where each one stops being reliable.

 - Guarantee data accuracy, transparent methodology, and results that hold up under scrutiny.

Measurement Partners & Ecosystem

 - Own Vibe’s integrations with the measurement tools clients already use: MMPs, web pixels and conversion APIs, MMM, and third-party measurement partners.

 - Assess how those partners measure CTV, understand where their methodologies fall short, and influence how they evolve.

 - Represent Vibe’s point of view on CTV measurement externally, through case studies, co-marketing with partners, and industry conversations.

Reporting & Activation

 - Own advertiser-facing reporting (dashboards, outcome metrics, exports) that makes CTV performance clear to both technical and non-technical buyers.

 - Close the loop between measured outcomes and campaign optimization, so better measurement leads to better performance.

 - Use SQL and log-level data to validate methodologies, size opportunities, and prioritize by impact.

What You Need

 - Deep, hands-on knowledge of attribution, conversion lift / incrementality testing, and MMM: how each works, what each is good for, and where each breaks (especially for CTV, where click-based models don’t apply).

 - Real expertise in the measurement ecosystem: how MMPs, pixels, clean rooms, MMM vendors, and third-party measurement partners work, and how their methodologies differ.

 - You’ve built measurement products, as the PM who owned them. Having used measurement outputs, or built general analytics or reporting tools, isn’t the same thing.

 - Solid statistical literacy: experimental design, holdouts, significance, confidence intervals.

 - Staff-level scope: you’ve owned a product area end to end, set its direction without being told what to build, and influenced engineering, data science, and commercial teams without direct authority.

 - Hands-on SQL and comfort in technical, data-intensive environments.

 - The ability to explain complex methodology simply and honestly to marketers, executives, and partners.

Nice to Have

 - You’ve owned a pixel or conversion API product (data collection for attribution).

 - CTV or video advertising experience.

 - Experience at a measurement or attribution company.

 - Experience with retail purchase data or foot-traffic / store-visit outcomes.

Why This Role

 - You’ll own the product domain that decides whether clients trust their Vibe spend, and whether they scale it.

 - You’ll have a direct line to revenue, because measurement is Vibe’s main lever for retaining and growing clients.

 - You’ll shape how an entire category proves CTV as a performance channel.

 - You’ll have high autonomy and influence across functions, from data science to clients’ C-suite.

Our Values

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

title: Head of Product, Enterprise
text:
A Note From the Founder
I have built product at Citizen since the first line of code, and I am still in it every day. Now I build with agents, and so does the rest of the company. Engineering, operations, and finance already run this way. The gap between an idea and a working build on my phone is measured in hours, and it is changing how fast we move more than anything in our history.

The enterprise business is working. Cities, hospitals, campuses, and private security teams are buying the same real-time intelligence that made Citizen the #1 safety app in America, and they are renewing. The next step is scale: a product that gets a customer signed to live in days, an API and integrations that put Citizen inside the systems they already run, and packaging that lets a small team serve many more of them. That is a product leader's job, and I want to build it with you, next to me, every day.

You will hear no from me, and I expect to hear it back, with the data.

The Role
Citizen is the #1 safety app in the U.S. Every day, thousands of videos are captured live at the scene of real incidents and distributed in real time to people in every major American city. No other product, consumer or enterprise, has this.

Under the app is a real-time machine. First-responder radio in every market we cover, video arriving from the scene, a Mission Control floor deciding in seconds what a city hears, and alerts that reach a phone before the sirens do. That machine is becoming agentic, and the same signal that reaches a resident's phone is what a security director, an emergency manager, or a newsroom needs on their screen, with the context, the tools, and the delivery their job demands. Designing that product, for institutions that act in the real world in real time, is the job here.

You are the Head of Product, Enterprise: the enterprise products and consoles, the public API and how it is packaged and priced, the integrations that put Citizen inside the tools cities already run, and the path from signed contract to live customer. You report to the Founder. Sales owns the relationships and the contracts; you own the product and its velocity. Enterprise customers renew and expand on what ships, and that number is yours. A peer owns the consumer product; you share one codebase, one data platform, and one standard for what agents may decide.

You will build with agents rather than a team of product managers. The production work of product management, discovery synthesis, competitive reads, spec drafts, partner documentation, onboarding runbooks, the weekly pipeline and renewal read, is done by an agent team you build and operate. One person with the right systems and the right judgment can now carry what used to take a full product org. That is the job, and this is the first moment it has been possible.

Why Now
Citizen built the public safety category, and the institutions responsible for safety now want what the public already has. The enterprise business has customers, renewals, and a pipeline; what comes next is a product that scales as fast as the demand for it. The levers are known: time from signed to live, integrations that make Citizen part of the workflow, packaging that fits how a city or a hospital buys. The next step is one person who owns those levers end to end. Until recently that took a department. Now it takes agents, taste, and the nerve to decide.

How We Work
Every role at Citizen is two things: the craft, and the operation of AI to multiply it.

You are a product leader first. Judgment about what to build and what to kill. A feel for what people will open every day and what they will pay for. The ability to tell a founder with strong opinions that the data says otherwise.

Every function here runs with agents doing the production work. Engineering ships through them, operations runs on them, and the weekly read assembles itself. You will inherit that stack on day one and build your own on top of it. By month three, agents should be drafting your specs and assembling the weekly read.


This job is about decisions, not process: you own what gets built, working directly with the Founder. The agents produce the artifacts. You produce the decisions.

What You Will Build
Each of these is a system you design and operate, not a department you run.

Signed to live. The path from contract to a customer using Citizen every day: provisioning, geofences, user setup, training, the first week. You make it take days, with agents doing the setup and a human checking the result. Time from signed to onboarded is the first number you own.

The enterprise product. The consoles and alerts that a security director, an emergency manager, or a communications team uses on a bad day and on a normal one: what ships, in what order, and what we choose not to build. Specs come out of customer calls and the data, drafted by agents you direct, and prototypes are in front of a customer in days, not in a deck in weeks.

Design partners. A small set of customers who build with us. You choose them, put prototypes in front of them, and decide what becomes the product.

The API and its packaging. How Citizen's real-time intelligence is consumed by other systems, how it is priced, what the tiers are, and how a developer or an agent gets from docs to a working integration without a call. You own the public API as a product.

Integrations and partners. Citizen inside the systems cities already run: dispatch, camera networks, mass notification, the tools a campus or a hospital already pays for. You decide which integrations to build, in what order, and you get them live.

The listening loop. Every enterprise call, every support ticket, every renewal conversation, every lost deal: read daily, by agents, and turned into a standing proposal for what the product should do next. You decide what gets built. The proposal never waits for a research sprint.

Scaling advanced photonics demands test and measurement systems as sophisticated as the devices themselves. We are seeking an Optical Test Engineer to design, build, and validate the optical test infrastructure that ensures our products meet rigorous performance, yield, and reliability standards—from wafer-level characterization through integrated module validation. You will be the critical link between design intent and production reality, turning data into actionable insight across every stage of our manufacturing pipeline.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Partner with PIC design, electrical, mechanical and test teams to define requirements for production and develop test approaches for complex hardware
Design, build, and validate optical test systems including imaging, microscopy, polarimetry, profilometry, and interferometry
Compile and analyze data sets to identify trends in performance
Assist with validation activities, including performance characterization at the wafer-, die-, and integrated module level
Work with internal engineering teams and suppliers to identify drivers of performance, yield, reliability, and quality issues
Review designs for manufacturability; drive integration build flow, test operations, and execution readiness
QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, optical engineering, applied physics or an engineering discipline
2+ years of hands-on experience in optics, photonics, lasers, or test
Working knowledge of lasers, photodiodes, fiber optics, optical test/troubleshooting methods, and signal integrity fundamentals

1+ years of programming experience (e.g., C++, LabVIEW, and/or Python)

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
Master’s degree or PhD in electrical engineering, optical engineering, applied physics or an engineering discipline
Experience in optical lab or production environments with strong attention to detail
Proficiency with optical design/analysis tools (e.g., Zemax)
Experience integrating and testing electrical and/or avionics systems
Experience with documentation practices and configuration management
Hands-on experience with electro-optic wafer- and die-level test systems
Hands-on familiarity with optical/RF test equipment (e.g., spectrum analyzers, VNAs, VSGs, high-speed oscilloscopes, BERTs)
Experience writing test plans and procedures, and delivering go/no-go decisions with clear rationale
CAD proficiency (NX preferred)

title: Senior Design Engineer
text:
ABOUT MINERVA

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Customers like the NBA, Ramp, Wander, Hard Rock Stadium Group and Luxury Presence use Minerva to develop a better understanding of their customers and introduce AI specifically built to understand the customer into their commercial organizations. Our campaigns outperform other tools because we built the entire stack: from identity to enrichment to data integration as well as agents to action and report on the analysis.

We've raised $20M from The General Partnership, 8VC, Lingotto, NBA Investments, Topology Ventures, Future Positive, Background Capital and many others. Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.



DESIGN ENGINEERING AT MINERVA

 - We build in TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Base UI and Tailwind. We use Motion where movement earns its place.

 - Design happens in code first. Figma or Paper comes out when a sketch is faster.

 - Our users are marketers and the CMOs they report to. They work with consumer data at a scale most interfaces never have to carry.


THE ROLE

An agent can build a segment in minutes. A marketer still has to understand it, trust it and put budget behind it. Getting them there is an interface problem, and it's this job.

Minerva's agents handle a marketing team's most data-heavy work. What reaches the customer is a screen. That screen has to make complex data feel simple. It also has to make the output trustworthy, and good enough to use, so that it leads to a result.

A design engineer here doesn't sit between design and engineering. You own the quality of the product experience from concept to shipped software, and you use code as the design medium. The distinction is ownership, not skill overlap.

This is a senior individual contributor seat on the product engineering team.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Make complex data legible. Design and build the surfaces where marketers work with data on hundreds of millions of consumers. Understanding an audience should take seconds, not a data team.

 - Turn agent output into a decision. Decide how segments, models and measurement are shown and explained, so a marketer trusts them, enjoys using them and puts them in market.

 - Design in code. Prototype what a static mock can't express, like motion, keyboard flows and work an agent is still doing. Take the strongest version to production yourself.

 - Make the cost call. Decide when an animation earns its place, and when a component is a one-off versus a primitive the team builds on.

 - Own the design system. Build and maintain the components and patterns product engineering ships with, so every surface feels like the same product.

 - Own it after launch. You're accountable for how a surface feels in a customer's hands, not how it looked in review.


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Taste. This is the hardest one to write a bullet for, so we'll just say it: your work shows it. Sometimes it's restraint. Sometimes it's making dull data fun, getting clarity out of a user, or showing what a product does without giving away how.

 - Opinions you can defend. Your reasons come from first principles that matter to the person using the product, not from a model's suggestion.

 - Shipped work. You've designed and shipped production interfaces yourself. We don't care about titles or years. We care what you've built.

 - You fight for decisions, with others. You argue a call through with people who care as much as you do, and you let the better argument win.

 - Located in or willing to relocate to New York City.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - First 90 days: you've shipped your first major product surface end to end, and it's yours.

 - First 6 months: you've shipped and own several of the bigger product surfaces, and the design system is what product engineering builds with by default.

 - There's no single number. The measure is the surfaces you own and how they hold up in customers' hands.


COMPENSATION

$237,000–$265,000 base salary, depending on experience. Meaningful equity. Medical, dental and vision.

 


HOW TO APPLY

Skip the cover letter. Send us your portfolio link, and make sure it includes something you designed and shipped. Applications without one won't be reviewed.

 


WHERE WE WORK

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

title: Cryogenic Systems Engineer
text:
ABOUT FUSE

We are building one of the most potentially consequential companies of the century. Our mission is to accelerate the world's transition to fusion energy while safeguarding humankind. This is not a normal company. This is not a normal job. We are committed for the long term to win.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Fuse is constructing Z-Star, a next-generation pulsed-power facility. Z-Star requires two deeply integrated cryogenic systems: a high-vacuum cryopumping system and a 4 K target/liner cryogenic cooling system.

As the Cryogenic Systems Engineer, you'll design, commission, operate, and maintain both systems and serve as the facility's resident expert in cryogenic and vacuum science.




CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Cryopump System Design & Operations

 - Design, procure, install, and commission the multi-stage vacuum system for the Z-Star chamber, including turbomolecular roughing pumps, cryopump arrays, and associated gate valves, interlocks, and controls.

 - Define cryopump sizing, placement, and regeneration schedules to meet target base pressure and shot-repetition-rate requirements.

 - Develop and maintain vacuum protocols including chamber venting, backfilling with inert gas, and controlled pump-down procedures compatible with shot operations.

 - Monitor and trend vacuum performance; diagnose and resolve outgassing sources, virtual leaks, and pump degradation.

4 K Target Cryogenic System

 - Design and commission the liquid helium cryostat and cryogenic delivery system for liner/target cooling, including vacuum-jacketed transfer lines, LHe reservoir management, and temperature-control instrumentation.

 - Develop procedures for target loading, cool-down, hold time at 4 K, and rapid warm-up following a shot.

 - Characterize and minimize cryogenic heat loads from radiation, conduction, and parasitic pathways to maintain stable 4 K conditions through the target preparation window.

Cryogenic Infrastructure Management

 - Manage liquid helium and liquid nitrogen supply, storage dewars, and transfer operations on-site, including logistics, safety, and vendor relationships.

 - Maintain all cryogenic hardware: cryopumps, compressors, cold heads (Gifford-McMahon or Pulse Tube), transfer lines, pressure-relief systems, and monitoring instrumentation.

 - Develop and implement a preventive-maintenance program for all cryogenic and vacuum equipment aligned with the facility shot schedule.

 - Train facility operations staff on cryogenic safety procedures and emergency response.

Diagnostics & Instrumentation

 - Specify, install, and maintain cryogenic instrumentation: Cernox or PT-100 temperature sensors at multiple stages, capacitance manometers, ionization gauges, residual gas analyzers (RGA), and pressure transducers.

 - Integrate cryogenic-system monitoring into the facility control and interlock system.

Safety & Compliance

 - Author and enforce cryogenic safety procedures, including ODH assessments, pressure-vessel requirements, LHe handling, and cold-burn precautions, in compliance with applicable U.S. codes.

 - Perform pressure-vessel and cryostat inspection and documentation per applicable ASME/CSA standards.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Physics, or Chemical Engineering with demonstrated cryogenics specialization.

 - 2+ years of hands-on experience designing, operating, or maintaining cryogenic systems at liquid-helium temperatures (4 K) in a research or industrial facility.

 - Proficiency with cryopump systems including sizing, installation, and regeneration cycles.

 - Strong working knowledge of vacuum science and technology: pumping speed, conductance, outgassing, leak detection using He mass spectrometry, residual gas analysis, and pressure measurement.

 - Experience designing or operating liquid-helium dewars, cryostats, and VJ transfer lines.

 - Familiarity with cryogenic instrumentation including thermometry, pressure, flow, and liquid-level measurement from 4 K to 300 K.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with fusion energy, pulsed power, or particle-accelerator cryogenic systems, particularly high-voltage-isolated cryogenic assemblies.

 - Familiarity with MagLIF-type target cryostats or ICF cryogenic target-preparation systems.

 - Experience with Gifford-McMahon (GM) or Pulse Tube (PT) cryocoolers for closed-cycle refrigeration.

 - Knowledge of cryogenic safety standards including ASME Section VIII, CGA G-5.4, ODH analysis procedures, and pressure-relief system design.

 - Experience with large vacuum-chamber systems (>10 m³) in a pulsed or repetitive-shot experimental facility.

 - Proficiency in thermal modeling and simulation using ANSYS, COMSOL, or equivalent tools.




WHAT WE VALUE

title: Inventory Specialist
text:
About Vital Lyfe

Vital Lyfe is a tech company redefining water autonomy through innovation, creating a new category of personal water making technology built to scale where infrastructure can’t.

Mission

The Inventory Specialist is responsible for supporting shop operations by managing the receipt, storage, kitting, and issuance of materials, parts, and hardware. The position ensures inventory accuracy, material traceability, and compliance with established procedures while maintaining proper stock rotation, documentation, and housekeeping. The role also supports operational metrics through cycle counting and consistent material handling practices.

What You'll Do

 - Receive, organize, and distribute raw materials, components, subassemblies, and hardware in support of shop floor operations

 - Store materials in designated bins, drawers, and racking systems, clearly labeling parts and storage locations

 - Adhere to established material handling procedures to ensure accuracy, safety, and compliance

 - Pick and assemble kits of required parts, materials, and hardware, confirming completeness and availability prior to release

 - Inspect incoming materials against accompanying documentation to verify part numbers, quantities, revisions, and absence of damage

 - Issue materials using approved documentation, ensuring required serialization, traceability, and lot verification are completed prior to release

 - Follow all applicable procedures, desk instructions, and standard operating guidelines

 - Track shelf-life controlled items and ensure proper stock rotation

 - Contribute to departmental and organizational performance metrics and objectives

 - Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area

 - Conduct cycle count activities to support inventory accuracy

Minimum Qualifications

 - High school diploma or equivalency certificate

 - 1+ years of inventory control experience

Preferred Skills and Experience

 - 3+ years of inventory control experience in a warehouse

 - Experience operate a forklift and other related inventory equipment

 - Experience and understanding of inventory and kitting processes

 - Excellent computer skills including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)

 - Experience within the aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, or electronic fields

 - ERP system experience (SAP, Oracle, etc.)

 - Bachelor’s degree

Physical Requirements (with or without reasonable accommodation)

 - Lift and carry up to 50 lbs. unassisted

 - Ability to work in warehouse and production areas with routine lifting, carrying, and movement of materials.

 - Must be able to climb ladders and be comfortable working in tight spaces.

 - Must be able to move repetitively, bend or twist, and use hands to handle, control, or feel objects, tools or controls.

 - Work involves standing and walking for extended periods. Suitable seating is provided when the nature of the work reasonably permits.

 - Wear required PPE (safety glasses, gloves, safety shoes) in production areas. Required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety shoes, will be provided or reimbursed by Vital Lyfe.

Why Vital Lyfe

 - Real world impact: Our mission is turning any water source, including ocean water, into safe drinking water. We're tackling one of humanity's most pressing challenges.

 - Aerospace DNA: Founded in 2024 by former SpaceX engineers, we bring aerospace manufacturing discipline to water technology.

 - Strong backing: Supported by investors including General Catalyst.

 - A product people want: Our first product, Access, is a push-button portable system that makes drinking water from seawater and other sources.

 - Get in early: We're a small, fast-growing team, so your work shows up in every unit we ship and there's room to grow with the company.

Benefits

 - Competitive Equity

 - 100% Medical, dental and vision insurance

 - 3 weeks paid vacation

 - 12 paid holidays

 - Parental Leave

 - 401k option (the company does not currently offer matching)

 - HSA/FSA plans

 - $50 Monthly Connectivity Reimbursement

 - $15 daily lunch stipend

Location Requirement: Ability to work 100% onsite in Torrance, CA (remote or hybrid work will not be considered)
